An old observation ID replayed after falling outside that tail is not recognized and can be appended again even with a single writer. Existing single-record and concurrent-admission oracles cannot justify an unqualified globally-exactly-once archive claim. Treat exactly-once as bounded-window until an authorized Gemini-only implementation provides persistent identity tracking or a documented retention guarantee. new_no_network_test_contract.pytest_source:
from part2.capital_flow.contracts import FlowObservation
from part2.capital_flow.storage import append_observations, load_observations

def test_archive_replay_outside_dedup_window(tmp_path):
    path = tmp_path / "observations.jsonl"
    fields = dict(family="etf", metric="net_flow_usd", asset="BTC",
                  value=10.0, unit="USD", effective_at_ms=1800000000000,
                  available_at_ms=1800000000000, observed_at_ms=1800000000000,
                  source="offline_fixture")
    a = FlowObservation(**fields, source_record_id="a")
    b = FlowObservation(**fields, source_record_id="b")
    assert append_observations(path, [a], max_existing_records=1) == 1
    assert append_observations(path, [b], max_existing_records=1) == 1
    assert append_observations(path, [a], max_existing_records=1) == 0
    assert [r.observation_id for r in load_observations(path)] == [
        a.observation_id, b.observation_id]
